body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{crit}}\) establish, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\), that the variable-coefficient smoothed gradient Green response has the frozen-pole logarithmic covariance, that the second elliptic term of \(\mathcal D_P\) and its harmonic term \(\mathcal H_P\) have bounded \(L^2\) scores, that coefficient, pole, and selected-lift plug-in errors are \(o(L_n^{1/2})\) in score norm, and that the nonlinear nested remainder is \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\)?
body.justification: This is the first-class open analytic content; without all four controls, the proposed covariance and feasible inference are unsupported.
body.gap: ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT reports that its coefficient-freezing error is of leading order in dimension two. Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 of GonzalezSanzShengWuAvellaMedina2026Influence prove the contamination Green response and pole singularity, but not the shrinking-bandwidth nested stochastic remainder.
body.consumer: A positive resolution supplies the reusable critical-plane module needed by every subsequent limit, covariance, and lower-bound theorem in the project.
